name: Editorial
thesis: The app should read like a publication: one clear voice, strong hierarchy, and room for the content to breathe.
bestFor: Reading, writing, news, research, journals, and newsletters.

variants.name: Broadsheet
variants.summary: A confident front page: oversized masthead, an asymmetric lead story, and a tight news list.
variants.signature: A hairline rule that runs past the content margin.
variants.treatment: Oversized serif masthead, uppercase kickers, a two-column lead, and a dense but orderly list.

variants.name: Field Notes
variants.summary: A working notebook: ruled lines, mono labels, compact entries, and a sense of use.
variants.signature: A ruled margin with numbered sections.
variants.treatment: Smaller serif display, mono metadata, ruled separators, and a compact rhythm.

variants.name: Literary Journal
variants.summary: A quiet journal: centered serif, generous leading, and a single pull quote.
variants.signature: A drop cap on the opening paragraph.
variants.treatment: Centered composition, large serif display, wide leading, and very few rules.

signatureMoves: A hairline rule that runs past the content margin.
A drop cap on the first paragraph.
A section number set in the margin.
An oversized pull quote that breaks the column.

platform.ios: NavigationStack with a large title. Use a serif display face for the masthead and SF Pro for body and metadata. Keep the system back button and swipe-back. Put one secondary action in the toolbar. Use a tab bar only when three destinations are true peers. Sheets use medium and large detents.
platform.android: TopAppBar with a small title after scroll and an edge-to-edge list. Use Noto Serif for display and Roboto for body. Consume insets. Use a NavigationBar only for three to five peers; otherwise use a rail. Do not add a FAB. Ripple belongs to rows, not to the whole card.

principles: One lead story per screen. Everything else is secondary.
Type and rules carry hierarchy; shadows are for overlays only.
Margins are part of the composition, not leftover space.
Real headlines and real bylines, never lorem ipsum.
avoid: A grid of identical cards with equal visual weight.
A hero image with a gradient overlay and no editorial reason.
Centered body text wider than 75 characters.
Decorative serif used for dense data.

content.title: The quiet infrastructure of everyday life
content.subtitle: A weekly dispatch on the systems we stop noticing.

items.title: The last mile is a design problem
items.body: Why the final ten metres decide whether a city feels close or far.

items.title: A small history of the receipt
items.body: Paper, proof, and the ritual of being able to return something.

items.title: What a library knows
items.body: A branch librarian on catalogues, quiet, and public trust.

screens.home: Masthead, issue metadata, one lead story with a two-column headline, then a tight list of secondary stories. The lead is twice the visual weight of any other item.
screens.detail: A 60-70 character measure, a serif headline, a byline and date, one pull quote, and related stories below a rule. Keep the reading position when returning.
screens.compose: A writing desk: title field, body editor, byline, a visible draft state, and one publish action. The keyboard must not cover the publish control.
screens.profile: A contributor page: portrait, short bio, a list of pieces, and one follow action. Do not use a dashboard of invented statistics.

components.button: Rectangular with a 2pt radius. Solid ink fill for the primary action; underline or text for secondary actions. No pills.
components.list: Hairline rules, 20pt vertical rhythm, no cards. Metadata sits above the title in uppercase 11-13pt with 0.08em tracking.
components.input: Underline only, label above, helper text below. No rounded box, no floating label.
components.navigation: iOS: large title plus tab bar for peers. Android: top app bar plus navigation bar or rail. The title is the strongest element in the chrome.
